headline: Margins widen and guidance rises despite a profit dip
summary_short: Circle's Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.6% y/y to $701M as RLDC margin expanded to 41% (+302bps) and Adjusted EBITDA grew to $143M, even as GAAP net income slipped 12.7% q/q to $48.2M and the company raised its FY2026 revenue and margin guidance.
summary_long: Reserve income rose 5% y/y as 25% USDC-circulation growth outweighed a 66bp yield decline; other revenue grew 41% on subscription/services. Distribution costs rose just 1% y/y, lifting RLDC margin to 41% (+302bps). Opex fell 56% y/y on lower IPO-linked stock comp, while Adjusted Opex rose 23% on product/AI investment. Net income of $48.2M fell 12.7% q/q (the y/y comparison, against the 2025 IPO quarter, isn't meaningful). USDC in circulation rose 19% y/y to $73.3B; CPN volume grew 76% q/q. Circle raised FY2026 Other Revenue guidance to $310-330M (from $150-170M, includes ARC presale revenue) and RLDC margin guidance to 41.7-43.7% (from 38-40%); Adjusted Opex guidance held at $570-585M. Cash rose to $1.73B.

drivers.explanation: Reserve income rose 5% y/y as a 25% increase in average USDC in circulation outweighed a 66bp decline in the Reserve Return Rate; other revenue grew 41% y/y on subscription and services growth.
Distribution, transaction and other costs rose just 1% y/y (mostly higher distribution payments) while revenue grew faster, lifting RLDC to $289M from $251M a year earlier.
Margin expansion is fully explained by revenue growing faster (+7% y/y) than distribution and transaction costs (+1% y/y), per the release's own cost breakdown.
Growth reflects revenue growth from higher USDC in circulation, partially offset by increased investment in costs related to new products, per the release.
Increase primarily driven by continued investment in product development, infrastructure, and AI capabilities, per the release.
Sequential decline reflects operating expenses rising faster q/q ($242M to $254M) than revenue (+1% q/q); the release narrates only y/y moves, not this q/q change.

Tracks the lower operating income, partly offset by other income rising to $17.9M from $11.7M q/q; the y/y comparison against the 2025 IPO quarter isn't meaningful and isn't addressed by a q/q narrative in the release.
Tracks the operating-income decline, partially offset by higher other income q/q ($17.9M vs $11.7M); not explained by any q/q narrative in the release.
Sequential decline tracks lower net income against a nearly flat basic share count; the release gives no q/q explanation for this move.
Sequential decline tracks lower net income against a nearly flat diluted share count (268.6M vs 266.7M); the release gives no q/q explanation for this move.
MD&A attributes the cash build to $538.5M of six-month operating cash flow, including $222.0M of ARC token presale proceeds, exceeding investing and financing outflows.

The y/y increase is largely a base effect of the June 2025 IPO (preferred-to-common conversion, ~$583M IPO proceeds, ~$445M follow-on) that predates this quarter, plus retained earnings and RSU/warrant issuances since.

The y/y increase reflects the June 2025 IPO's preferred-to-common conversion and follow-on share issuances, both predating this quarter; the q/q change (266.7M to 268.6M) is modest, from RSU vesting and warrant exercises.

Management said results reflect the current rate environment and a slowed crypto market, both outside Circle's control, while pointing to its new federal trust bank charter, Arc's September 16 mainnet launch, and expanding institutional USDC use as forward drivers.
